slides.headline: Long day in the field? Your body knows
slides.sub: Where massage fits for weekend cricketers, from bowlers to keepers.

slides.title: Bowlers: back, hips and trunk
slides.body: Bowling loads the lower back, trunk and hips heavily. Massage can ease tightness through the glutes, back and sides after a long spell, alongside the strength work that helps you bowl.

slides.title: Keepers: hips and thighs
slides.body: Hours of squatting behind the stumps leave hips, quads and calves tired. Massage on a rest day plus some hip mobility can help the next match feel easier on your legs.

slides.title: Fielders: shoulders and hamstrings
slides.body: Throwing from the boundary and sprinting between the wickets load the shoulders and hamstrings. A focused session can help these areas feel looser between weekends.

slides.title: Book it for the right day
slides.body: Lighter massage a day or two after the match tends to suit most players. Leave deeper work for midweek so your legs feel fresh by Saturday's first ball.

slides.title: Massage is part of the plan
slides.body: Massage complements warm-ups, strength work and hydration in the heat. Sharp pain, swelling or a back that's worse each week is worth a physio assessment.

slides.headline: Cricket legs feeling every over?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists tailor each session to your role on the field and refer to our physios when needed. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Six hours in the field on a 35-degree Saturday? Your body keeps score. 🏏

Weekend cricket asks different things of different players. Bowlers load the back, trunk and hips. Keepers spend hours in a squat. Fielders throw and sprint after long periods of standing still.

Remedial massage can help tired, tight areas feel looser between matches. Lighter work a day or two after the game tends to suit most players, with deeper sessions kept for midweek. It works alongside warm-ups, strength training and staying hydrated in the heat.

Sharp pain, swelling or a back that's getting worse each week is worth a physio assessment.
